name: a verification loop draws beside a condensed before/after pipeline
looks: A headline states that verification sits in the loop, not after it. On the left, a small circular diagram of review, QA and build steps draws itself as a cycle. On the right, a grey row of many small pipeline steps (the old way) sits above a short, green, condensed row (the new way), making the shrink obvious at a glance.
build: The cycle's nodes and connecting arc draw on clockwise with strokeDashoffset, each node landing as its segment completes. The before row is a flex line of many small static chips; the after row tweens in from the same starting chips, merging and shrinking to fewer, wider, green-filled chips on power2.inOut.
sound: A soft tick per node on the loop, a low hum through the draw, a satisfied chime as the condensed row settles.
prompt: Claim that a safeguard runs continuously rather than as a final step. Draw a small circular loop diagram of that safeguard's stages on one side, and beside it, shrink a long row of many small steps (the old way) into a short, bright row of far fewer steps (the new way), so the contraction itself proves the claim.
